arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Ms. Hammoud argued that the opposing side's concession narrows the dispute.
She contended that a modified approach ignores state court deference.
Ms. Bahal asserted that both legal standards have been met in this case.
She stated that the state did not seek review of the prejudice finding.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case examines how federal courts handle habeas corpus petitions. The core issue involves the interaction between two legal standards. One standard assesses prejudice from constitutional errors. The other standard grants deference to state court judgments. The parties disagree on how these standards interact. The Court must clarify the procedural path for these reviews.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: the side that brought the case wants the Court to confirm that the Brecht standard alone governs this review.
the opposing side wants the Court to require application of the AEDPA deference standard as well.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: the side that brought the case argues that the Brecht standard subsumes the AEDPA requirements in this context.
the opposing side argues that the AEDPA standard remains a separate and necessary precondition for relief.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the procedural burden for federal habeas courts. It determines whether judges must apply two distinct legal tests. The outcome shapes the difficulty of obtaining federal relief. It affects the finality of state court judgments. The ruling clarifies the scope of federal judicial review.
